fact: The 'forerunner of the dog' — it rises just before Sirius to announce the Dog Star.
bio: Procyon (Alpha Canis Minoris) is a nearby white main-sequence star only 11.5 light-years away, orbited by a faint white-dwarf companion. Its closeness makes it the eighth-brightest star in the sky despite its modest true luminosity.
cultural: The Greek name means 'before the dog', because from many latitudes Procyon climbs above the horizon shortly ahead of Sirius. With Sirius and Betelgeuse it forms the bright 'Winter Triangle'.
